mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals strengthening economic demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, or GDP growth is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE increases by > 0.5pp, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and SPX returns is positive over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply-side constraints, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face higher costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO decreases by > 1%, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) increase simultaneously by more than 2% month-over-month, it signals robust demand, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and investment rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by > 2%, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in one month signals labor market contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000, or the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and SPX returns is positive over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS > 4%, or the joint effect of CPIAUCSL increases and high FEDFUNDS is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals robust supply-side growth, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and efficiency.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following a 3-month INDPRO increase of > 2%, or INDPRO growth is not significantly correlated with SPX returns over a 5-year period.
